reason: Both conversations correctly and honestly identify normal pan-resonance induction noise with no part or engineer needed, and neither crosses a safety line. Conversation 1 wasted its first turn on a pointless 'unplug for ten minutes' step (then withdrew it), but it then asked the single most diagnostic question - try other pans on the same zone - and confirmed the noise follows the cheap cookware, giving the homeowner concrete evidence and sensible advice to use heavier flat-based pans. Conversation 2 reached the same conclusion from the low-power dependence but suggested a confusing 'hand on the pot while switched off' test that the homeowner rightly could not make sense of, and it never actually established pan-dependence, instead simply asserting it; its 'use a smaller pot' tip is also slightly off given the base already undersizes the ring. Repetitive boilerplate safety panels in 1 are a minor negative, so the edge is only slight.
